prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a beginner site that (A) explains crypto in plain English and (B) runs a real portfolio and publishes its actual P&L (including losses)? Or do you mean a site that is simply very transparent about industry losses/hacks and shows real on‑chain numbers?

Most mainstream beginner sites explain things clearly but do NOT run a public trading account and publish their losses. If you want both plain English and verifiable numbers you usually need to combine two types of resources: a beginner explainer and a data/dashboard source that shows on‑chain or fund performance.

Short answer / quick recommendations
- Plain‑English beginner explainers
  - Coinbase Learn — very approachable, clear basics.
  - Coin Bureau — in‑depth, plain English guides and videos.
  - Bankless — great for DeFi explained in everyday language.

- Sites that show real numbers (on‑chain, dashboards, transparency)
  - Glassnode — on‑chain metrics and clear charts (real data).
  - Dune Analytics — community dashboards showing raw queries and real numbers (you can view anyone’s public dashboards).
  - Nansen — wallet‑level analytics (paid), great for seeing real flows/positions.

- For candor about mistakes, hacks and losses
  - The Defiant — focus on DeFi, covers hacks/losses and explains impacts plainly.
  - Chainalysis blog — transparent incident reports and data on thefts/losses.

Why there’s no single perfect site
- Very few reputable beginner sites publish their own trade journal with full P&L and losses — that’s a transparency practice more common with specific traders/bloggers or some funds that choose to publish audited performance.
- If you want someone who posts their trading trades, wins and losses, look for individual Substacks/YouTube creators who explicitly maintain a public trade journal (and verify via linked public wallets when possible).

If you want, I can:
- Recommend specific individual bloggers/YouTube channels that publish trade journals and losses, or
- Put together a short learning path that pairs a plain‑English guide + a handful of Dune/Glassnode dashboards so you learn concepts and see the raw numbers behind them.

Which of those do you mean/prefer?
